drafted_from: tool row in tools/office-files/tool-rows.json, do-work/rewrite-office-open-xml-cells.py and test/decode-office-open-xml.test.py (run on its fixture)
start_here: Say to your AI: "In /work/budget.xlsx change the price text from $2,499 per seat to $100/month bundle, and make the 999 in the formula say n/a, writing /work/budget-new.xlsx." It writes a rules file, runs rewrite-office-open-xml-cells.py on your computer and reads the new file back.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads or rewrites one file on the person's own computer and prints what it found or changed.
instructions: 1. Read the file first with tool:read-an-office-file so you know the cell text, formulas and sheets.

2. Write a rules file (a JSON list): each rule has kind (cell, shared-string or document-text), match (formula_contains, value_equals, text_contains, or equals and contains for words) and set (formula, formula_replace, value, text_replace, text or replace).

3. The AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: tool:change-cells-or-words-in-an-office-file} and runs its `run` command with the file, rules and a new output path. Read the report: a rule with matched 0 changed nothing, so fix the rule.
4. Read the new file with tool:read-an-office-file to confirm what it holds before saying it is done; the input file is never changed.

worked_examples.title: Change a price and a formula in a workbook
worked_examples.ask: In /work/budget.xlsx change the price text to $100/month bundle and make the 999 in the formula say n/a, writing /work/budget-new.xlsx.
worked_examples.given: From tools/office-files/test/decode-office-open-xml.test.py; I ran its rewriter on that fixture to observe the report. Command: python3 -I tools/office-files/do-work/rewrite-office-open-xml-cells.py /work/budget.xlsx /work/rules.json /work/budget-new.xlsx, where rules.json is [{"kind":"cell","match":{"formula_contains":"999"},"set":{"formula_replace":["999","\"n/a\""],"value":"n/a"}},{"kind":"cell","match":{"text_contains":"$2,499"},"set":{"text_replace":["$2,499 per seat","$100/month bundle"]}},{"kind":"cell","match":{"text_contains":"never present"},"set":{"text_replace":["x","y"]}}] and the workbook is the one tool:read-an-office-file's kit reads.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"rules":[{"index":0,"kind":"cell","matched":1},{"index":1,"kind":"cell","matched":1},{"index":2,"kind":"cell","matched":0}],"written":"/work/budget-new.xlsx","warning":"rules matched nothing: 2"} Reading budget-new.xlsx with --formulas then gives B1 "Price is $100/month bundle" and B2 value "n/a" with formula IF(A2>0,"n/a",A2); A1 and A2 are as they were.
